evidence.estrutura: Height worked through national civil-rights organizations and local coalitions, favoring cooperative institutional reform rather than a distinctive centralization doctrine.
evidence.representacao: Voting rights, political participation and coalition leadership strongly support representative democracy and inclusion.
evidence.poder: Her civil-rights work opposed legally enforced racial hierarchy and state-tolerated discrimination, favoring rights constraints on coercive power.
evidence.imigracao: Her coalition politics emphasized racial and social inclusion; this supports pluralism more than assimilation, though immigration policy was not a central field.
evidence.diplomacia: Her work was primarily domestic civil-rights activism, with no strong military foreign-policy doctrine; a moderate diplomatic orientation is safest.
evidence.intervencao: No strong doctrine on foreign intervention is established; her rights-based politics do not justify an extreme.
evidence.economia: Anti-poverty, employment and economic-opportunity work support a center-left social-policy orientation within a mixed economy.
evidence.controle: She favored public programs and anti-discrimination enforcement rather than command planning; moderate regulation.
evidence.comercio: No distinctive trade doctrine is established.
evidence.religiao: Height worked through institutions including the YWCA and had religious roots, but her public program was civic rather than theocratic.
evidence.moral: Racial equality, women’s rights and civic inclusion strongly support socially progressive positions.
evidence.tecnologia: Technology was not a defining political issue; moderate.
